forms.detail: EUDA: south-west Asian heroin, the more common form, is a brown powder, usually the free base.
EUDA: south-east Asian heroin, less common, is a white powder in the form of the hydrate hydrochloride salt (CAS 1502-95-0).
DEA: a white or brownish powder, or a black sticky substance known as 'black tar heroin'; AIHW: powder or rock form (Australia).
EUDA: crude diamorphine base may be used directly, purified further or converted into the hydrochloride salt.
EUDA: in opioid agonist treatment, diacetylmorphine (heroin) and slow-release morphine are more rarely prescribed than methadone and buprenorphine.
